extraction.name: Instruction-Following Eval (IFEval)
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models using a set of prompts containing verifiable instructions.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by identifying 25 types of verifiable instructions and creating around 541 prompts. Prompts were generated using few-shot prompting to identify illogical prompts and rephrase them for diversity, followed by manual curation and editing.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Synthesized prompts containing verifiable instructions, created via few-shot prompting and manual curation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Prompts were generated by concatenating base prompts with verifiable instructions. Illogical prompts were removed using few-shot prompting. Prompts were rephrased to increase diversity. Manual checks and edits were performed.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Verification of instruction following was performed using strict and loose accuracy metrics. Loose accuracy involved transforming responses (e.g., removing markdown font modifiers, intros, outros) to reduce false negatives.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Instructions were verified using deterministic programs. Two metrics were used: strict accuracy (direct string/heuristic match) and loose accuracy (matching after applying transformation functions to the response).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The loose verification process reduces false negatives but may introduce false positives. The strict metric is considered the primary criterion, with loose accuracy as a complement.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple verifiable instructions per prompt (1 or more).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automated verification scripts using string matching and transformation functions (e.g., removing markdown syntax).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Ensuring LLMs can consistently adhere to given directives is crucial for safety and reliability, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human evaluations are noted to have potential biases and inconsistencies. The proposed method aims to be unbiased and automatic.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively; edge cases exist where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed. The current implementation can be improved by increasing diversity/quantity of instructions and extending to multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation benchmark for Large Language Models (LLMs) to assess instruction-following proficiency.
